subject: Canada
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Canada–United States border. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). Wikipedia says the border is "commonly said" to be the longest undefended border; the episode does not claim that as fact.

claims.text: The Canada–United States border is the longest international border in the world by total length.
The boundary, including the boundaries on the Pacific coast, Great Lakes and Atlantic coasts, is 8,891 kilometres long.
There are two international borders between Canada and the United States: with the northern tier of the contiguous United States (6,416 km) and with Alaska (2,475 km).
The border is commonly said to be the world’s longest undefended border; it is not militarized, although civilian law enforcement is present.
